title: 第 39 課｜非慣性參考系：慣性力從哪裡來｜Landau–Lifshitz 經典力學
description:
到目前為止所有的討論都在慣性系裡：一個質點在外場中的拉格朗日量是 ½ m v₀² 減去位能，由它得到的運動方程也只在這種座標系裡成立。在非慣性系裡會怎樣？最小作用量原理本身與座標系無關，拉格朗日方程照樣成立，要改寫的只有拉格朗日量本身，而這件事分兩步做。第一步換到以速度 V(t) 相對慣性系平移的參考系。兩個速度差一個 V，代進去多出兩項：½ m V² 只依賴時間，是個全微分，可以直接丟掉；中間的 m v′ · V 也拆成一個全微分加上一項帶有參考系加速度的部分，把全微分丟掉之後剩下乾淨的拉格朗日量 ½ m v′² 減去 m W(t) · r′ 再減去位能，其中 W 是 dV/dt。所以加速的平移完全等效於一個均勻力場，大小是質量乘加速度、方向相反——加速車廂裡的擺就沿著 g 減 W 的方向掛著。第二步再加一個原點相同、以角速度 Ω 轉動的參考系。平移系裡的速度等於轉動系裡的速度加上 Ω 與位置的叉積，代進去就得到適用於任意參考系的拉格朗日量。值得注意的是轉動帶來一項與速度成一次的項 m v · (Ω × r)，這是以前任何拉格朗日量都沒有的。取它要求的導數代入拉格朗日方程，運動方程裡出現三個慣性力：m r × dΩ/dt 只在轉動不均勻時存在；2 m v × Ω 是科氏力，它與所有非耗散力都不同，依賴質點的速度，所以慣性系裡的一條直線在轉動系裡看起來是彎的；m Ω × (r × Ω) 是離心力，位於 r 與 Ω 張成的平面內，垂直於轉軸並背離它，大小等於 m ρ Ω²，其中 ρ 是到轉軸的距離。後兩個即使轉動完全均勻也存在。

本影片為《Landau–Lifshitz 經典力學》教學系列第 39 課（繁體中文版）。

title: Lesson 39 | A Non-Inertial Frame: Where the Inertia Forces Come From | Landau–Lifshitz
description:
Everything so far has been done in inertial frames: for one particle in an external field the Lagrangian is one-half m v-squared minus the potential energy, and the equation of motion that follows from it holds only in such a frame. What happens in a non-inertial frame? The principle of least action does not care which frame we choose and Lagrange's equations still hold, so only the Lagrangian itself has to be transformed, and that is done in two steps. First take a frame translating with velocity V of t relative to the inertial one. The two velocities differ by V, and substituting adds two terms: one-half m V-squared depends on the time only and is a total derivative, so it can be dropped, while the middle term m v-prime dotted into V also splits into a total derivative plus a piece carrying the acceleration of the frame. Dropping the derivative leaves the clean Lagrangian one-half m v-prime-squared minus m W of t dotted into r-prime minus the potential energy, where W is dV/dt. An accelerated translation is therefore exactly equivalent to a uniform field of force equal to the mass times the acceleration and pointing the opposite way, which is why a pendulum in an accelerating carriage hangs along g minus W. Second, add a frame with the same origin rotating with angular velocity Omega. The velocity in the translating frame is the velocity in the rotating one plus Omega crossed with the position, and substituting gives the Lagrangian for any frame at all. Notice that the rotation adds a term linear in the velocity, m v dotted into Omega crossed r, which no earlier Lagrangian contained. Taking the derivatives it calls for and putting them into Lagrange's equation, three inertia forces appear in the equation of motion. The first, m r crossed with the rate of change of Omega, exists only when the rotation is non-uniform. The second, twice m v crossed with Omega, is the Coriolis force, and unlike every other non-dissipative force it depends on the velocity of the particle, so a straight line in the inertial frame curves away in the rotating one. The third, m Omega crossed with r crossed Omega, is the centrifugal force: it lies in the plane of r and Omega, points perpendicular to the axis and straight away from it, and its magnitude is m rho Omega-squared, where rho is the distance from the axis. The last two survive even a perfectly steady rotation.

Lesson 39 of the Landau–Lifshitz Classical Mechanics teaching series (English edition).
